title: Body systems
ks3: Structure and function of living organisms
intro: Your heart, lungs, bones and muscles all work together. Learn how you breathe, how blood moves and how your skeleton and muscles let you move.
description: Free KS3 Biology questions with answers on body systems: the heart and blood, the lungs and breathing, the skeleton, joints and muscles. Marked instantly, for Year 7, 8 and 9.

options: Takes in oxygen from the air
questions.hint: It's a muscle that never stops.
questions.explain: The heart is a muscle that pumps blood around the body through blood vessels.

questions.q: Which blood vessels carry blood **away** from the heart?
questions.explain: Arteries carry blood away from the heart. Veins carry it back. Capillaries are tiny vessels in between.

questions.q: Blood carries oxygen and glucose to the cells. What does it carry away from them?
questions.hint: It's a waste gas from respiration.
questions.explain: Cells make carbon dioxide in respiration. Blood carries it to the lungs, where we breathe it out.

questions.q: Why does your heart beat faster when you run?
options: Your muscles need more oxygen and glucose for respiration
questions.explain: Working muscles respire faster, so they need more oxygen and glucose. The heart pumps faster to deliver them.

questions.q: Which organs take oxygen into the body from the air?
questions.explain: In the lungs, oxygen passes from the air into the blood.

questions.q: In the lungs, what are the **alveoli**?
options: Tiny air sacs where gases move in and out of the blood
questions.hint: They look like tiny bunches of grapes.
questions.explain: Alveoli are tiny air sacs with thin walls and lots of blood vessels, so oxygen and carbon dioxide can move between the air and the blood.

questions.q: Which gas is there **more** of in the air you breathe out than in the air you breathe in?
questions.explain: Breathed-out air has more carbon dioxide (and less oxygen), because your body has used oxygen and made carbon dioxide.

questions.q: When you breathe in, what does the diaphragm do?
options: Contracts and moves down, so the chest gets bigger
questions.hint: A bigger space inside the chest means lower pressure, so air rushes in.
questions.explain: The diaphragm contracts and flattens (moves down) and the ribs move up and out. The chest gets bigger, so air flows in.

questions.q: Why is smoking harmful to the lungs?
options: Tar and chemicals damage the alveoli and airways
questions.explain: Cigarette smoke contains tar and harmful chemicals that damage the airways and alveoli and can cause diseases such as lung cancer.

questions.q: Which of these is **not** a job of the skeleton?
questions.hint: Bones hold you up and keep you safe.
questions.explain: The skeleton supports, protects and helps movement. It also makes blood cells in the bone marrow. It doesn't digest food.

questions.hint: It's the bony case of your head.
questions.explain: The skull protects the brain. The ribs protect the heart and lungs.

questions.q: About how many bones are in an adult human skeleton?
questions.explain: An adult has about 206 bones. Babies have more, because some bones join together as you grow.

questions.q: What kind of joint is your knee?
questions.hint: It bends one way, like a door.
questions.explain: The knee is a hinge joint: it moves back and forth in one direction. The hip and shoulder are ball and socket joints.

questions.q: To bend your arm, which muscle contracts?
options: Neither: bones move on their own
questions.hint: The biceps is on the front of your upper arm.
questions.explain: The biceps contracts to bend the arm while the triceps relaxes. To straighten it, the triceps contracts. Muscles that work like this are called antagonistic pairs.

questions.q: Why do muscles have to work in pairs?
options: Muscles can only pull, not push
Bones need two muscles to stay warm
questions.hint: A muscle can get shorter, but can it push?
questions.explain: Muscles can only pull by contracting. So one muscle pulls a bone one way, and another muscle pulls it back.
